To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prevalence of HIV, HBV, HCV and syphilis was high in refugees in Bari.
the prevalence of HBV and HCV markers was 8.3% and 4.5% respectively, whereas the HIV prevalence was 1.5%.
the prevalence of HBsAg and anti-HBc in refugees was 8.3% and 45.6%, respectively, while the prevalence of anti-HCV was 4.5%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the health of refugees and migrants, and the need to provide them with adequate health care.
the health of refugees in the Asylum Centre and with the need for a suitable screening program to prevent the spread of infectious diseases.
the health of refugees and the need to protect the Italian population from infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a high prevalence of infectious diseases, especially of HBV, HCV and HIV, is present in the refugee population.
the study population was at high risk of infection with hepatitis B, hepatitis C and syphilis, with a prevalence of infection with HIV of 1.5%.
the presence of a large number of subjects who are carriers of infectious agents with a potential for transmission through the blood or sexually is an alarming situation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prevalence of HBsAg, HCV and HIV in the refugee population in Bari is high and the VDRL prevalence is low.
the refugees in the Asylum Centre in Bari, Palese, Italy are at high risk for infectious diseases.
the prevalence of HBV, HCV and HIV in this population of refugees is similar to the prevalence in the general population in the area where the refugees are living.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prevalence of infectious markers among refugees is high, and this should be taken into account when designing public health policies.
the presence of infectious diseases among refugees is a public health issue and that it is essential that a screening programme for the early diagnosis and treatment of these diseases is carried out.
the screening of infectious diseases should be carried out in all asylum seekers and refugees, as well as the screening of blood-borne and sexually transmitted infections.
